rationale:
bugs_open/457's fix shipped 2026-09-03 (f895616d7, council 13273c8c APPROVED) and is live in the running chassis 239ab3626. It closed the INSERT half of the defect and left the other half armed. This submission narrows one cell of its decision table.

The original defect: findBlogListingSlot has four exit paths; the caller read `existingComponentID != uuid.Nil` as 'this slot is free' when it only ever meant 'strategy 1 fired'. The fix made every path read occupancy and made the write decision a pure function of (origin, occupants). Correct, and it stopped the append.

What it left: decideBlogListingWrite tests `Occupants == 1 -> opUpdate` BEFORE it consults Origin, so the origin gate governs only opInsert. On a slot resolved by strategy 2b's guess or strategy 3's default, the single occupant is NOT the listing - it is whatever the page legitimately keeps in that slot. 'Refreshing the listing' therefore OVERWRITES it. That is the same unauthorised structural edit the append was, with a worse verb: the append added a row nobody asked for; the update destroys a row somebody did.

The inconsistency is visible inside the shipped fix's own test file. TestBlogListingRefusesToInventASlotFromAGuess refuses a guessed origin when the slot is EMPTY, reasoning that 'a guessed slot name is by construction NOT a listing slot - strategy 1 or 2a would have matched if it were. Creating a listing there is a silent structural edit to someone else's page.' That reasoning applies with more force when the slot is OCCUPIED, and there the old table wrote. The safer case was being refused and the more damaging one permitted.

This is not a return to the root-cause bug. That bug used a question about the RESOLVER ('did strategy 1 fire') as a proxy for a question about the DATA ('is anything here'). Occupancy is still read on every path and still decides refresh-vs-create. Origin decides a different question that was never asked: whether anything authorises a write here at all. Both must be answered; only one was.

It is live-armed, not theoretical. boxingonline.com /articles/index.html is the motivating page. It resolves `generic-text-block` by 2b and holds 7 rows in that slot today, so it currently refuses as ambiguous. site_delivery_and_editor is about to delete the six orphan rows (bugs_open/457 fix candidate 4, owner-assigned to them). The moment they do, occupancy falls to 1 - the page's own prose block at position 2, which carries a real component_id - and the next rerender-pages run overwrites that prose with the article listing. The remediation for this bug is what arms it.

Blast radius measured, not assumed. Of the 4 live blog-index pages, 3 match strategy 1 (ai-agent-orchestration.com and leopardessconsulting.co.uk on `blog-listing`, finetuning.uk on `article-grid`), so they resolve as slotOriginExistingRow and are untouched by this change. boxingonline is the only page that reaches 2b at all, and its behaviour today (refuse-ambiguous) is identical before and after. So this change alters the outcome on ZERO pages today and prevents a wrong write on ONE page as soon as the cleanup lands. The disconfirming result would have been a blog-index page resolving via 2b or 3 with exactly one occupant today, whose listing would stop refreshing; there is none.

The refusal must not error, and does not: rebuild_blog_listing is an unconditional step of rerender-pages between render_site_components and get_pages, and that workflow declares no error_step, so an error return aborts the run before create_rerender_items and creates none of the ~18 page rerenders. That IS the outage this bug was filed for. The new arm returns opRefuseNoSlotAuthority, which the caller already handles by logging at Error and returning rebuilt:false.

plan.summary: bugs_open/457's shipped fix (f895616d7, council 13273c8c, live in chassis 239ab3626) made the blog-listing write decision a pure function of (origin, occupants), but tests Occupants==1 -> opUpdate BEFORE consulting Origin, so the origin gate governs only the INSERT arm. On a slot resolved by strategy 2b's guess or strategy 3's default, the single occupant is not the listing but whatever the page legitimately keeps there, so 'refreshing the listing' overwrites it. This moves the Occupants==1 test inside the Origin switch, so exactly one cell changes: a guessed or defaulted origin with one occupant now refuses instead of overwriting. Measured 2026-09-04, this alters the outcome on zero pages today and prevents a wrong write on boxingonline.com /articles/index.html the moment site_delivery_and_editor deletes this bug's six orphan rows — which is the owner-assigned remediation for this very bug, and is what arms it.

edits.rationale: One cell of the decision table changes: (guessed|defaulted origin, exactly 1 occupant) goes from opUpdate to opRefuseNoSlotAuthority. Every other cell is bit-identical. The unknown-occupancy and >1-occupant arms stay ahead of the switch, so the ambiguity and swallow guards are untouched. The refusal text distinguishes 'refusing to overwrite the row that occupies it' from the existing 'refusing to invent one', because the two cases need different remedies from whoever reads them: one is a duplicate to clean up, the other is a page plan missing a listing section.

This test asserted the behaviour being changed, so it must change - and it is my own lane's earlier assertion, so the correction is recorded in place rather than edited away, per the working-docs rule. What the test was RIGHT about is kept: the loop still covers BOTH slotOriginExistingRow and slotOriginPlanListing, so the mutation it names (making the update arm conditional on Origin == slotOriginExistingRow alone, i.e. restoring the root-cause proxy) still kills it. Only the two unauthorised origins move out.

Pins the new cell in both directions and asserts the refusal text says 'overwrite', so the two refusal causes stay distinguishable to a reader. Mutation-proven 2026-09-04: reinstating the `if slot.Occupants == 1 { return opUpdate }` line ahead of the switch fails it on both origins with 'got 1' (opUpdate) and on the missing 'overwrite' wording; restoring the change returns the package to green. The test carries the live case and the blast-radius measurement in its comment so the next reader does not have to re-derive why only one page is affected.

grounded_in: decideBlogListingWrite, as shipped: `if slot.Occupants == 1 { return opUpdate, "" }` sits ABOVE `switch slot.Origin`, so the origin gate reaches only opInsert and opRefuseNoSlotAuthority.

The shipped fix's own test comment, TestBlogListingRefusesToInventASlotFromAGuess: 'A guessed slot name is by construction NOT a listing slot - strategy 1 or 2a would have matched if it were. Creating a listing there is a silent structural edit to someone else's page, repeated once per run, which is how six orphans accumulated in two days.'

bugs_open/457, CONTRIB from site_delivery_and_editor: strategy 2b 'returns generic-text-block with uuid.Nil' on boxingonline because its sections are [hero, generic-text-block, call-to-action] and none is listing-class.

Only boxingonline reaches 2b.

Result: 6 'Latest Articles' headings, 36 article-card__title, 14 empty article-card__category, 2 empty article-card__excerpt - identical to the pre-fix baseline recorded in bugs_open/457, i.e. the damage is unchanged.

plan.risks:
1. IT NARROWS A COUNCIL-APPROVED DECISION AND CHANGES ITS TEST. The prior round approved 'update the single occupant whatever strategy named the slot' and pinned it with a test whose named killing mutation is 'make the update arm conditional on Origin == slotOriginExistingRow'. That mutation is NOT what this does: the update arm stays open to slotOriginPlanListing too, so the named mutation still kills the (renamed) test. Reviewers should check that claim directly — if the narrowing had gone one origin further it WOULD be the regression the prior round guarded against, leaving a plan-declared listing permanently unrefreshed.

2. A LISTING THAT LEGITIMATELY LIVES IN A NON-LISTING SLOT WOULD STOP REFRESHING. If some page keeps its real article listing in a slot named nothing listing-class, and that slot is reached only by 2b, this change freezes it. Measured 2026-09-04: 3 of the 4 live blog-index pages match strategy 1 and never reach 2b; the fourth (boxingonline) has 7 occupants and already refuses. So the population is empty today. It is a fact about current data, not an enforced invariant, and the check is one query: any blog-index page whose slot resolves by 2b/3 with exactly one occupant. THIS IS THE DISCONFIRMING RESULT — a non-empty answer means this change strands a working listing and should be reconsidered.

3. THE REFUSAL IS ONLY LEGIBLE IN A LOG. A refused page's listing silently stops being rebuilt, and the only signal is the action's Error line plus rebuilt:false in the step result. This is the open item the shipped fix already names ('the discovery check that should FILE the gap'), and this change makes it bite on one more page. It is deliberately NOT smuggled in here — it needs its own item_type, handler and register entry. Reviewers may reasonably object that the two should land together; the counter-argument is that the wrong write is live-armed by an imminent data cleanup, and a work item nobody reads is not worth delaying the guard for.

4. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX. It does not repair the six orphan rows (owner-assigned to site_delivery_and_editor), and it does not give boxingonline an article listing: after the cleanup that page's plan still names no listing section, so it will correctly serve no list until a listing section is added to pages.sections. Refusing is the honest outcome, not a complete one, and it must not be read as a fix for the served page.
